new_finding_mirror_divergence.summary: While the head was advisory, it closed ONLY the first account of a bybit_2 / bybit_portfolio twin, never the mirror. 3 of 3 twinned exit-head closes diverged. That breaks the Stage-2 invariant ('the mirror carries IDENTICAL trades'), and the Gate-2 demotion signal read off bybit_portfolio was not measuring the leg the live account actually traded.
new_finding_mirror_divergence.root_cause: INFERRED, not observed in live logs: src/runtime/exit_head_shadow.py::maybe_score_exit_head dedups on seen_key = (model_id, order_package_id, bar_ts) (L477-480). Twins share one order_package_id, so the monitor's call for the SECOND account returns None, and exit_head_verdict(None) -> no close. Reproduced locally (scratch script, no src change): same pkg id, two accounts -> [('bybit_2', {'stage': 'advisory', 'would_exit': True}), ('bybit_portfolio', None)]. The divergence in the trades table is MEASURED. That the dedup CAUSED those three historical divergences is inferred from the mechanism reproduction plus the data. Not verified: that both twins' monitor calls run in the same process with a shared _SEEN set on the same bar. No live log line ties a specific close to the dedup.
new_finding_mirror_divergence.paired_sum: head arm -0.097R vs no-head twin +10.299R -> head -10.40R over n=3. R = (exit - entry) / (entry - stop_loss) from the trades rows, GROSS, with each account's own entry. n=3 is anecdotal, and one 12.1R TP dominates it. It is stated because it points the same way as the replay's paired delta below, not because it establishes anything alone.
new_finding_mirror_divergence.tier: Tier-2 (runtime order path). Proposed fix: key the dedup per account, e.g. (model_id, account_id, pkg_id, bar_ts), or cache the rec per (model_id, pkg_id, bar_ts) and return the cached rec to every twin. Add a test for the twin case. This must land BEFORE any re-promotion. It is inert while every exit-head artifact is shadow.

caveats: POPULATION MISMATCH, and it is decisive. recovered_R = head_simulated_net (353 full-window trades) minus evidence net_r_oos (73 OOS trades from a different record). scripts/research/exit_head_attribution_result.py L169-170 subtracts a 73-trade figure from a 353-trade figure. The like-for-like paired statistic in the SAME payload is delta_gross_r = -34.92R (head-on 8.38R vs head-off 43.30R net over the identical 353 trades). By the unit's own declared design ('PAIRED: the head-on and head-off arms score the same decision bars', RQ-20260922-007.yaml power.basis), the head is net-NEGATIVE by ~34.9R, about -0.099R per trade.

n=353 is the FULL window and NOT out-of-sample. The artifact was fit on 1662 trades / 34338 rows with train_window_present=false (train_start/train_end null), so the replay window almost certainly overlaps the training data. In-sample bias favours the head, so an OOS delta is expected to be no better than -34.9R.

Cost modelling: both arms charge each trade the fee_r of its ORIGINAL (un-replayed) exit (grader docstring L33-45), so the delta is effectively gross. Funding saved by earlier exits is not credited. That is small next to 34.9R and cannot flip the sign.

Live anecdote, same direction: the three bybit_2/bybit_portfolio twins where only bybit_2 took the head's exit came out at -10.4R for the head (n=3, gross). Live bybit_2 exit_head closes total -1.13 USD at tiny size.
Drift: the last reads before the demote showed ks 0.2018 / psi 0.9637, both significant (W4, 2026-09-25). The artifact has not been re-trained since 2026-07-12.
Unregistered: gate-check cannot evaluate this model, so there is no ladder gate report to lean on.
